root_cause.text: In `dw_pcie_ep_raise_msix_irq()`, a PCI posted write (`writel`) to raise an MSI-X interrupt may not complete before the outbound ATU entry is unmapped, causing the in-flight write to target unmapped memory or trigger IOMMU faults.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds a `readl(ep->msi_mem + offset)` after `writel(msg_data, ep->msi_mem + offset)` and before `dw_pcie_ep_unmap_addr()` to flush the posted write. The commit log states: "Flush the write by performing a readl() of the same address to ensure that the write has reached the destination before the ATU entry is unmapped." The CVE description also describes the race and shows IOMMU errors from the unmap happening too early.

candidates.rationale: This posted write may not complete before the ATU is unmapped, leading to the write targeting unmapped memory.
Unmapping the ATU entry while a posted write is still in flight causes the write to hit unmapped memory or trigger IOMMU faults.
Returning success immediately without ensuring the posted write has completed allows the vulnerability to manifest.
